name: Historical failures
outstanding_work: Establish the full pre-2019 history of water quality issues at Willawarrin/Bellbrook - this register now reaches back to June 2019 (CHR-0007) but no further. Confirm the exact start date of the 2019/2020 trucked-water period. RUN-0015 added general (non-water-specific) settlement history from Kempsey Shire Council's own heritage record (SRC-0036, fetch-blocked): Willawarrin was part of the Toorooka pastoral lease from 1842, gained its first hotel in 1893, and was an important livestock-selling centre 1949-1970 - useful background predating this thread's water-specific evidence by well over a century, but still no source found addressing water-quality problems specifically before June 2019. RUN-0016 found a substantial, specifically-dated gap-filler between CHR-0007 (June 2019) and CHR-0001 (late Oct 2019): the Carrai East Bushfire accelerated 8 November 2019 and forced an evacuation via Bellbrook Public School on 11 November 2019 (SRC-0037, fetch-blocked, cross-confirmed across two searches with named officials/individuals). This is very likely the specific bushfire event behind EV-0002/EV-0003's cited 'drought, bushfire, and subsequent heavy rainfall' cause, but a real preserved primary source is needed before it can be promoted to an Evidence Register/Chronology entry. RUN-0019 found that the same fire event is also the subject of an active NSW Coronial Inquiry into a resident's death (SRC-0039, fetch-blocked) - recorded strictly as sourced factual reporting of coronial-inquiry proceedings, with no finding of fault or responsibility by any person or body stated or implied. Willawarrin also had its own evacuation point (Willawarrin Hall, per search-snippet detail not yet independently registered) distinct from Bellbrook's school-based one. RUN-0027 (operator directive: "all evidence must go into register as found"): promoted SRC-0036, SRC-0037/SRC-0038, and SRC-0039 to EV-0019/EV-0020/EV-0021 respectively, each at verification_state "Requires Verification" with a documented hash_exception_reason (search-snippet sourced, DEC-0008 fetch outage), rather than holding them at Source Register level pending future preservation. RUN-0033: identified the official NSW Coroners Court findings document (SRC-0060, "Court Decision" type) for the Carrai East Bushfire/Barry Parsons matter already covered via media at SRC-0039/EV-0021 - a stronger primary-source type once fetchable. Per search snippet, adds the fire's likely cause (lightning strike, ~16 October 2019) and scale (238,601 hectares, 90+ homes and 250+ outbuildings damaged/destroyed), and the date findings were delivered (27 March 2024). RUN-0037 (deep research pass on Bellbrook/Q-0002): found a significant, previously unknown episode - Bellbrook's water supply was contaminated by arsenic/heavy metals from 2005 (EV-0043), and water had to be trucked into the town in 2008 as a result (EV-0044), a full decade before the case's well-documented 2019-2020 crisis. This would make 2008 the EARLIEST documented Bellbrook water-supply failure in this register, predating even CHR-0007 (June 2019 restrictions). Sourced to a single historical-summary page (historicalencounters.org), reproduced consistently across three separate searches but not yet corroborated by a genuinely independent, contemporaneous source - flagged as the priority next lead for this thread. RUN-0038: attempted to independently corroborate EV-0044's 2008 Bellbrook trucked-water claim via Trove/OldNews (the Macleay Argus's own newspaper archives, 1885-present, SRC-0070) and further targeted searches - found that the 2005-2007 arsenic-detection portion of the story IS independently corroborated (a Council source reproduces it near-verbatim, EV-0046), but the specific 2008 trucked-water claim remains single-sourced. General web search cannot query into newspaper-archive sites' individual scanned pages; a future run or manual researcher searching Trove/OldNews directly for a 2008 Macleay Argus article is the clearest remaining path to confirm or disconfirm EV-0044. RUN-0041: MAJOR NEW FINDING - a second, major bushfire directly impacted Willawarrin in October 2023 (the Willi Willi Fire, 46% of the Shire burned, 340 structures damaged/destroyed, one fatality, formal disaster declaration and a dedicated recovery centre at Willawarrin - EV-0051/EV-0052/EV-0053), previously completely unknown to this register. This directly parallels the 2019 Carrai East Bushfire's established causal chain (bushfire -> ash/sediment -> river contamination -> trucked water) and is the clearest, highest-priority new lead in the whole investigation: the next run should specifically search for any Willawarrin water-supply disruption in the weeks/months following 16 October 2023, which would be a FOURTH documented trucked-water/contamination episode (after 2008, 2019-2020, and the FY2020-21 intermittent periods) if confirmed. RUN-0042: three dedicated search attempts to establish whether the October 2023 Willi Willi Fire (EV-0051) also triggered a Willawarrin water-supply disruption found no relevant change - the same 2019-2020 recap content (already registered as SRC-0044/EV-0024, a December 2023 Council FAQ) kept resurfacing, and was correctly NOT re-registered as new 2023-specific evidence, avoiding the same stale-content conflation trap already caught once at RUN-0028. Did register a specific, dated confirmation of the fire's direct rural-property impact at Willawarrin itself (BlazeAid/Need for Feed relief operations at the Showground, EV-0054). Whether the fire caused a water-quality/carting disruption remains a genuinely open, unconfirmed question - the two most promising unexplored documents for this specific window are SRC-0052 ("Kempsey Year in Review 2023-24") and the still-unfetched SRC-0047/SRC-0042 annual water quality reports, none of which have yielded content via search snippets despite repeated attempts across multiple runs. RUN-0043: the operator provided the full text of SRC-0068 (historicalencounters.org's Bellbrook page) directly, which this session's fetch tool could not retrieve. Preserved and hashed it, upgrading EV-0043/EV-0044/EV-0045's sourcing from search-snippet-only to an actual document (EV-0055) - though the page itself attributes its content to Wikipedia, so this remains short of full independent corroboration, particularly for the 2008 trucked-water claim specifically. Also captured substantial new pre-1900 Bellbrook history (European settlement 1830s and early conflict with the Dunghutti/Thunggutti people, postal and school history - EV-0056) and the 1885 Aboriginal Protection Board reserve (EV-0057). Flagged an unresolved minor discrepancy: this source dates Bellbrook's naming to 1882, while EV-0018 gave 1892 for its gazettal. RUN-0049 (operator directive: continue DWMS annual reports): re-mined the already-preserved SRC-0042 (2020-2021 DWMS report) for its remaining unextracted Executive Summary content - found that Willawarrin, Bellbrook, and Clybucca reservoirs were cleaned/inspected by external contractors during 2020-2021 with no integrity breaches found, and that both towns recorded 2 "dirty/cloudy water" customer enquiries each that year (EV-0063). Searched again for the still-unfetched, higher-priority 2019-2020 DWMS report (SRC-0047, the crisis year itself) and for any 2021-22/2022-23/2023-24 DWMS reports - found no evidence a DWMS annual report was published for any year after 2020-2021 under the same naming convention; Council appears to have shifted to less formal "Water update" pages (SRC-0080/SRC-0083) for subsequent years. SRC-0047 remains the single highest-priority unfetched document in this whole investigation. RUN-0050 (operator directive: find the DWMS Annual Report series' new name/department): confirmed the "Drinking Water Management System Annual Report" title (SRC-0042/SRC-0047) was discontinued after the 2020-2021 edition. It has been succeeded by a leaner "Drinking Water Quality Result Summary" format (filename pattern "water-testing-results-YYYY-YYYY.pdf"), still published by the same Water & Sewer department using the same NSW Health-sponsored verification monitoring program - not a different department, just a reformatted/renamed report. Found the 2023-2024 edition (SRC-0091), which directly covers the Willi Willi Fire year - the single most promising remaining lead for this thread's standing "did the fire cause a Willawarrin water crisis" question, though no Willawarrin/Bellbrook-specific figures could be extracted from search snippets this run. Could not find a 2021-2022 or 2022-2023 edition under this same naming pattern - either a genuine ~2-year public-reporting gap exists between the last DWMS report and the first "water testing results" summary, or earlier editions exist under a still-undiscovered name. RUN-0051 (operator directive: "10 years of editions"): found a THIRD naming convention for this report series - an older "dwms-annual-wq-report-1819-final.pdf" pattern, giving a 2018-2019 pre-crisis baseline edition (SRC-0093), the earliest one found; no 2017-2018 or earlier edition could be located under any of the three known naming patterns despite dedicated searches, suggesting this may be the first published edition. More importantly, found the structural source ALL these reports are drawn from: Council's own descriptions state its water quality data is "reproduced from the NSW Government Drinking Water Database" (NSW Ministry of Health, SRC-0092) - a single, ongoing government repository behind every yearly Council PDF, though it is unclear from search snippets alone whether it offers direct public querying or is an inter-agency tool only. Separately, a search for "10 years of editions" surfaced a distinct, unrelated document set worth explicitly noting as excluded: a "water-epa-data" directory of dated lab-result batches (e.g. "24/2558", "23/1089") is Council's SEWAGE TREATMENT PLANT effluent/discharge monitoring under its 7 EPA pollution licences - wastewater quality, not drinking water supply quality - correctly not treated as part of this thread's report series despite superficial naming similarity. RUN-0052 (operator directive: "naming convention changes is evidence"): promoted the naming-convention/URL-pattern instability finding from RUN-0050/RUN-0051 to a first-class Evidence Register entry (EV-0065), rather than leaving it only in this thread's narrative. Confirmed via further dedicated search that no 2021-22 or 2022-23 edition exists under any known naming pattern - the apparent two-year publication gap remains unexplained and unresolved. RUN-0059: found a genuinely new, dated shire-wide response confirming the Willi Willi Fire period coincided with a real water-stress management episode - Level 1 water restrictions, 16 October 2023 (same date as the fire's start) to 9 February 2024, including a temporary tightening then relaxation of public filling-station access rules (EV-0069/CHR-0031). This is drought-attributed and shire-wide, not a confirmed Willawarrin-specific trucked-water disruption, so it does not resolve this thread's standing question - but it is the first concrete, dated evidence of ANY documented water-supply-management response during this exact window, where previous runs found only silence.

name: Trucked water
outstanding_work: RUN-0024 found SRC-0044 (fetch-blocked): Council carted water to Willawarrin 'since October 2' (2019) and 'intermittently' to Bellbrook and the Thunggutti Aboriginal Community during the bushfire emergency - the first source confirming Bellbrook actually received trucked water, not just anticipated need. SRC-0045 (fetch-blocked) adds volume/cost detail: $161,000 government funding, approximately 10-13 kilolitres/day carted to each village. RUN-0025 specifically searched for a separate Bellbrook start/end date and found none - every source treats Willawarrin and Bellbrook as returning to river supply together on 18 June 2020 (CHR-0002), and describes Bellbrook's carting as 'intermittent' rather than continuous from a single date, consistent with SRC-0044. Working conclusion (not yet primary-sourced): Bellbrook's trucked-water period likely did not have a single clean start date the way Willawarrin's did, and ended on the same date as Willawarrin's. Still needs a preserved primary source before this can be promoted to an Evidence Register entry. RUN-0027: promoted SRC-0044 and SRC-0045 to EV-0024/EV-0025 (Willawarrin trucked water from 2 October 2019; Bellbrook and Thunggutti received intermittent carting; $161,000 funding; 10-13 kL/day per village), same "Requires Verification" / search-snippet-sourced basis as the rest of this run's promotions. RUN-0031: the operator-supplied SRC-0042 full text adds substantial new detail. Bellbrook's plant was offline specifically from 13 January 2020 to 18 June 2020 due to persistent high manganese (EV-0032), giving THR-02 its first exact primary-sourced start date for Bellbrook's own outage (distinct from Willawarrin's, dated from 2 October 2019 per EV-0024/SRC-0044). Beyond the main 2019-2020 crisis, both towns needed further, separate trucked-water periods during FY2020-21 alone: Willawarrin on 30 October-2 November 2020 (a turbidity incident, EV-0033) and intermittently 23 Dec 2020-11 Jan 2021 and 18 Mar-13 Apr 2021; Bellbrook intermittently 22 Dec 2020-7 Jan 2021 and continuously 21 Mar-30 Jun 2021 (EV-0034). This substantially strengthens the "recurring failure" premise with primary-sourced, dated instances beyond the single well-known 2019-2020 episode. RUN-0037: if EV-0044 (2008 trucked water at Bellbrook due to arsenic contamination) is confirmed against an independent source, this establishes THREE separate Bellbrook trucked-water episodes across the historical record (2008, 2019-2020, and the further intermittent 2020-21 periods at EV-0034) rather than the single well-known 2019-2020 crisis - materially strengthening this case's "recurring failure" framing. Not yet promoted beyond "Requires Verification" pending independent corroboration. RUN-0048 (operator request: "find trucking logs"): re-read the already-preserved SRC-0042 text closely for genuine operational-log detail rather than just summary dates. Found a precise total-duration figure - Willawarrin's supply "was under water carting for 240 days" during 2019-2020 (EV-0061) - and an actual timestamped internal incident log for the July 2020 Bellbrook event, plus the specific named reservoir ("Greenhill Reservoir") water was carted from for the October 2020 Willawarrin incident (EV-0062). Searched separately for a literal water-carting contract/tender or company-level cartage log: found no source naming a specific contractor for the 2019-2020 or 2023-24 carting operations, but identified three unfetched leads that could resolve this - Council's own GIPA Register of Government Contracts for 2023-24 (SRC-0086, the closest thing to a formal trucking-contract disclosure log found), the 2019-2020 Annual Financial Statements (SRC-0087, which would likely itemise water-carting as a discrete expense line for the crisis year itself), and a real local water-cartage business, Macleay Valley Water Cartage (SRC-0088) - explicitly NOT confirmed as the contractor used for this case, registered only as evidence such local capacity exists.

name: Iron contamination
outstanding_work: Obtain actual water-quality test results (iron concentrations vs Australian Drinking Water Guidelines) rather than descriptive media/council reporting only. RUN-0026 found a previously unregistered Council annual water quality report covering the exact July 2019-June 2020 crisis period (SRC-0047, fetch-blocked) - the strongest candidate yet, alongside the already-registered 2020-2021 report (SRC-0042), for actual concentration figures. No specific figures found via search-engine snippets; both documents need to be fetched directly. RUN-0031: the operator directly supplied the full text of SRC-0042 (the 2020-2021 DWMS Annual Report), which this session's own fetch tool could not retrieve (DEC-0008). This finally closes the thread's central gap with actual measured data: Willawarrin recorded 0 Iron ADWG exceedances that year (9 tests, NSW Health program) but was the only one of Council's 8 supply systems whose total ADWG/WQI exceptions increased year-on-year (14 in 2019-2020 to 43 in 2020-2021, against 105 in 2018-2019) - see EV-0031/EV-0035. The still-unregistered 2019-2020 report (SRC-0047) covering the actual crisis period remains the next priority if it can be obtained the same way.

name: Manganese contamination
outstanding_work: Obtain actual water-quality test results (manganese concentrations vs Australian Drinking Water Guidelines) rather than descriptive media/council reporting only. RUN-0026 found a previously unregistered Council annual water quality report covering the exact July 2019-June 2020 crisis period (SRC-0047, fetch-blocked) - the strongest candidate yet, alongside the already-registered 2020-2021 report (SRC-0042), for actual concentration figures. No specific figures found via search-engine snippets; both documents need to be fetched directly. RUN-0031: the operator directly supplied the full text of SRC-0042. Willawarrin recorded 4 Manganese ADWG aesthetic exceedances in 2020-2021 (0.159-0.2 mg/L against the >0.1 mg/L aesthetic guideline, 20 Nov-14 Dec 2020, 26.67% of that year's 15 Manganese tests under the operational monitoring program) - see EV-0031. This is aesthetic-only (no exceedance of the higher 0.3 mg/L health guideline was recorded), and the separate NSW Health-sponsored program's 13 Manganese samples that year averaged much lower (0.0141 mg/L) with zero exceedances - both figures are reported honestly rather than picking the more dramatic one. Bellbrook's five Free Chlorine Alert Levels that year were separately attributed to high manganese consuming chlorine residuals, though no Bellbrook Manganese ADWG exceedance was itself recorded. The still-unregistered 2019-2020 report (SRC-0047) covering the actual crisis period remains the next priority.

name: River conditions
outstanding_work: Obtain WaterNSW or Council river-flow/dam-level data for the Macleay River and Steuart McIntyre Dam across the 2019-2020 drought and since, to move beyond descriptive reporting. EV-0009 (June 2019) adds that the Sherwood Borefield depends on uncontrolled upper-catchment river flow and that Steuart McIntyre Dam's usability as a supply source was itself in question at that time. RUN-0028 found a genuinely new, dated 2023 drought-response event (SRC-0048/SRC-0049, EV-0028): the main Kempsey/Lower Macleay network switched from the Sherwood Borefield to the Steuart McIntyre Dam around 25 August 2023 due to declining river flow. This is the main-network equivalent of, but distinct from, Willawarrin/Bellbrook's own supply problems - checked and ruled out a second Willawarrin/Bellbrook-specific trucked-water crisis in 2023, which traced back to a stale CMS "page updated" timestamp on the 2019/2020 articles (SRC-0002/SRC-0003) rather than a real event. RUN-0033: identified a peer-reviewed academic publication (Johnston et al. 2022, Water Research) presenting actual flow-stratified water quality data for the Macleay River across the 2019-2020 drought/fire/flood period - the first Scientific Publication source type used in this register, and a stronger source type than the general project-level media coverage already at SRC-0028. Confirms major water-quality parameters were highly elevated during the post-fire period, though iron/manganese specifically are not confirmed by any search snippet found. RUN-0034: found a significant, previously unregistered event - a Moderate to Major Flood Warning for the Macleay River around 21-22 May 2025, with Bellbrook's own gauge reaching a major flood level (10.55m against a 6.50m minor threshold) and Kempsey CBD flooding after levees overtopped (EV-0041). This sits chronologically between the Steuart McIntyre Dam plant's construction start (24 March 2025) and its confirmed "under construction" status as of 31 August 2025 (EV-0029) - a plausible, not yet confirmed, factor in that project's timeline. A separate, milder flood warning around 21 March 2025 was also found but not registered as a distinct evidence item pending clearer sourcing.

name: Extraction decisions
outstanding_work: Establish the specific extraction-point/bore-vs-river decisions made for Willawarrin (bore-reliant) versus the main Kempsey network (Steuart McIntyre Dam + Sherwood Borefield), and why Willawarrin was not connected to the more secure dam-fed system. RUN-0034: searched specifically for why Willawarrin remained on a standalone bore-based system rather than being connected via pipeline to the Steuart McIntyre Dam/Sherwood Borefield network, including for a Council options-assessment or feasibility report (SRC-0042's Implementation Plan mentions an "options assessment report endorsed by DPE" for the main KLM plant, a possible model for a similar Willawarrin-specific document, but no such document or its content could be found via search). No relevant change - this remains a genuine, search-exhausted gap requiring a council business paper or engineering report not indexed by search engines. RUN-0040: found a genuinely new, previously unexplored angle - Kempsey Shire Council joined the NSW Government's Regional Network Leakage Detection Project around June 2024 (EV-0048), a shire-wide leak-survey program distinct from the treatment-plant-capacity investment this case has centred on. Not yet confirmed whether it covered Willawarrin/Bellbrook's own reticulation specifically - a candidate angle for a future run investigating network condition/asset age as a contributing factor, alongside the still-unanswered bore-vs-pipeline question.

name: Funding

EV-0013 (May 2022) shows the project existed at least that early with no cost figure attached yet; SRC-0021 (Pump Industry Magazine) and SRC-0022 (Kempsey Council, 8 Aug 2024 - one day after EV-0004) are both blocked and are likely leads once manually retrieved. RUN-0023 added broader council-financial context (SRC-0043, fetch-blocked): Kempsey Shire Council recorded an $8.1 million general fund deficit for FY2024-25 (nearly double the prior year's ~$4m), following a November 2025 NSW Audit Office/external-auditor presentation to council - directly relevant to the case's original brief on whether Kempsey appears in NSW Audit Office at-risk-council reporting, though the specific 'Appendix 2' named-list question remains unconfirmed. RUN-0027: promoted SRC-0043 (Kempsey Shire Council's $8.1m FY2024-25 deficit, NSW Audit Office link) and SRC-0045 ($161,000 trucked-water funding) to EV-0023/EV-0025. RUN-0039: tried a ninth distinct angle for Q-0003 (comparing the 2024 tender scope to the 2025 final design, then Council's Long Term Financial Plan for a general cost-escalation explanation) - found only generic shire-wide financial pressure context (EV-0047), not a Willawarrin-specific cost driver. This question is now genuinely search-exhausted; the answer almost certainly sits in an un-indexed council business-paper item (a budget variation resolution) rather than anything reachable by further search-engine queries. RUN-0053 (operator directive: pursue paths not yet taken): found the first evidence directly addressing Q-0003's cost-increase question - Council increased the Willawarrin plant's funding deed value specifically "to accommodate cost increases from the competitive tender process" (EV-0066), per a National Water Grid Authority project page. Suggests pure tender-price escalation rather than an announced scope change, though this remains unconfirmed pending a preserved primary document. Also checked and explicitly rejected a search-summary claim of a distinct "Bellbrook Water Treatment Plant" capital-works line item - a second, independent search found no such project on Council's own Current/Completed Works pages (only Willawarrin and Crescent Head plants are named there), consistent with this thread's existing understanding that Bellbrook has not received dedicated treatment-plant infrastructure since 2020; the initial claim appears to have been an AI-search-summary error, not registered as evidence. RUN-0054 CORRECTION to RUN-0053: the operator reports personally having heard of a second/new Bellbrook water treatment plant in planning "for years," corroborating rather than refuting the search-summary claim RUN-0053 had treated as a likely AI-summarization error. On reflection, RUN-0053's dismissal was itself too hasty - the underlying search behavior (a confident claim with no quotable primary citation across five separate searches over two runs) is genuinely ambiguous, not a clean stale-content trap like RUN-0028/RUN-0042 - and should not have been characterized as "correctly rejected." Re-opened as a live, unresolved, operator-corroborated lead (see Q-0002) rather than a closed dead end. No document confirming a second Bellbrook plant has been found by this session as of RUN-0054; this remains unconfirmed, not established. RUN-0055 (operator directive: Section 60 approval records): found the actual regulatory mechanism and dataset (LWU Regulatory Approvals, SRC-0094) behind Willawarrin's "Section 60 endorsement" milestone, with a specific WAMS reference (14493) and a precise June 2022 concept-design endorsement date (SRC-0095/EV-0067). A dedicated search for an equivalent Bellbrook Notice of Determination in this same dataset found none. Council's Delivery Program 2022-2026 (SRC-0096) also names only Steuart McIntyre Dam, Crescent Head, and Willawarrin as its water infrastructure projects - no Bellbrook plant - the second Council document type in a row not to list one. The operator's reported lead remains open (per RUN-0054), but two further independent checks this run still found no citable confirmation.

name: Regional water security funding program (Steuart McIntyre Dam / Sherwood Borefield)
outstanding_work: New thread opened 2026-07-28 after EV-0005 revealed the Willawarrin plant is one component of a larger $52.9m regional package that also funds a new main treatment plant for Kempsey/Frederickton/Smithtown/Gladstone (~18,000 residents).
